summary: The nontrivial elliptic dilation semigroup has polynomial generator eigenvectors complete in every finite-p Hardy space and weak-star complete in H-infinity. The introductory universal negative claim is false; main non-elliptic theorems are not contradicted.

problems.title: Universal failure of elliptic eigenvector completeness

location.anchor: paragraph beginning It is here worth emphasizing

problems.claim: Elliptic analogues of the completeness questions invariably have negative answers because of a common fixed point.
assumptions_checked: phi_t(z)=exp(-t)z is a holomorphic disk self-map for t>=0
identity at zero time, semigroup law, compact-open continuity
0 is a common interior fixed point
f_n=z^n for all integers n>=0 are in H-infinity and all finite-p Hardy spaces
generator domain limit exists in each finite-p norm
problems.actual_result: C_phi_t z^n=exp(-nt)z^n; Gamma z^n=-n z^n; polynomial span dense in H^p, 1<=p<infinity, and weak-star dense in H-infinity via uniformly bounded Taylor approximations of radial dilates.
problems.counterevidence: Main theorems expressly assume non-ellipticity. Additive Koenigs relation does not apply to elliptic example; this is not a counterexample to Theorems 1.1–1.4.
problems.impact: Peripheral scope-setting assertion is false; no core theorem dependency demonstrated.
problems.correction: Restrict the additive formulation to non-elliptic semigroups and state that elliptic eigenvector completeness is separate and can hold.

problem_reviews.definitions_hypotheses_quantifiers: The p.3 frequency span includes lambda=0 and asserts negative answers for similar elliptic completeness questions. phi_t(z)=exp(-t)z is nontrivial, compact-open continuous, satisfies the semigroup law and fixes the interior point0.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: For every n>=0, C_phi_t z^n=exp(-nt)z^n and the norm derivative at t=0 is -n z^n in every H^p,1<=p<infinity. The span is all analytic polynomials, norm dense in H^p. For f in H-infinity, take r_j up to1, approximate f(r_j z) uniformly on the closed disk by a Taylor polynomial with error<=1/j; the polynomials are uniformly bounded by ||f||+1 and converge pointwise, hence weak-star. No H-infinity norm-strong continuity assumption is used.
problem_reviews.counterevidence: All nonconstant monomials vanish at0, but the constant eigenfunction and free linear coefficients remove any common-value obstruction to span density. The additive relation applies only to non-elliptic semigroups; interpreting it literally for elliptic maps gives no elliptic analogue and cannot establish a universal negative eigenvector statement.
problem_reviews.dependency_and_impact: The actual p.50 proof assembly uses hyperbolic and parabolic non-elliptic classifications, not the introductory elliptic claim. No core theorem counterexample or main-proof damage is established.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Restrict additive Koenigs-domain formulation to non-elliptic semigroups and state separately that elliptic eigenvector completeness may hold, as for dilation. Only that local introductory correction is verified.

independent_acceptance.coverage_honesty_review: The original scope excludes detailed Sections6-8 geometry, distinguishes finite-p norm completeness from H-infinity weak-star completeness, and limits the reviewed file to v3 without publisher equivalence. Original image-interface failures remain historical beside the later actual visual-continuation receipt; current scientific acceptance does not relabel the initial partial coverage as a whole-paper verification.
independent_acceptance.decision_explanation: The universal introductory claim of negative elliptic eigenvector completeness is refuted by the nontrivial dilation semigroup. The constant eigenfunction must be retained; the complete polynomial span and bounded radial-Taylor approximation prove both claimed kinds of completeness. The non-elliptic core theorems do not depend on the false assertion, so Minor and the stated local replacement are supported.
